(p-75) Sūrat al-Malā'ikah (The Angels)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to Allah﴾: He praised Himself to teach and to exalt (His creation).

﴿Originator of the heavens﴾: its initiator and its innovator. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "I did not know the meaning of *fāṭir* (originator) until two Bedouins disputed before me over a well, and one of them said: *anā faṭartuhā* (I originated it), meaning: *ibtadaʾtuhā* (I began it)."

﴿and the earth, who made the angels messengers﴾ to His servants.

﴿Possessors of﴾: *dhawī* (possessors). It is a collective noun (*ism jamʿ*) for *dhū*. It is either a substitute (*badal*) for *rusulan* (messengers) or an attributive adjective (*naʿt*) of it.

﴿wings﴾: the plural of *janāḥ* (wing).

﴿two, three, and four﴾: these are adjectives (*ṣifāt*) of *ajniḥah* (wings). They are not declined (*lam tanṣarif*) because of the repetition of *ʿadl* (deviation from the original form) in them. That is because they are deviated (*ʿudilat*) from the cardinal number forms into other forms, just as ʿUmar is deviated from ʿĀmir, and from repetition into non-repetition. It has also been said that the reason is *ʿadl* together with being a description (*waṣf*), and the reliance is upon this. The meaning is that among the angels there is a group whose wings are two by two, meaning each one of them has two wings; and a group whose wings are three by three, and perhaps the third lies in the middle of the back between the two wings, supporting them with strength; and a group whose wings are four by four.

﴿He increases in creation﴾: that is, He increases in the creation of wings and other things,

﴿what He wills﴾. It has been said that this is a good face, a good voice, good hair, good handwriting, and beauty in the eyes. The verse is unrestricted (*muṭlaqah*) and encompasses every increase in creation: height of stature, balance of form, perfection of the limbs, strength in grasping, soundness of intellect, firmness of opinion, eloquence of tongue, love in the hearts of the believers, and what resembles these.

﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾: capable.

(p-76) ﴿What Allah grants to people of mercy﴾: "mercy" (raḥma) is indefinite (nakkirat) to indicate generality and vagueness, as if He said: of any kind of mercy, whether provision, or rain, or health, or something else.

﴿none can withhold it﴾: no one is able to withhold it and hold it back. The word "opening" (fatḥ) is used metaphorically for releasing and sending forth. Do you not see His saying: ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾, that is, prevents and restrains?

﴿none can release it﴾: none can set it free

﴿after Him﴾: after His withholding of it. The pronoun referring back to the noun that carries the meaning of a conditional is feminine, in keeping with the sense of "mercy"; then it is made masculine, in keeping with the word it refers back to, since that word has no feminine form. The first was explained by "mercy," so it was fitting for the pronoun to follow the explanation, while the second was not explained, so it was left in its original masculine form.

And from Mu'adh, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The hand of Allah will not cease to be outstretched over this Ummah so long as its best do not show gentleness to its worst, its righteous do not honor its sinners, and its reciters do not aid its rulers in disobedience to Allah. When they do this, Allah withdraws His hand from them."

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾: the Dominant, the One able to send forth and to withhold.

﴿the Wise﴾: the One who sends forth and withholds according to what wisdom requires of sending and withholding.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 3:

﴿O people, remember﴾, with the tongue and the heart, ﴿the favour of God upon you﴾, which is what preceded: the spreading out of the earth like a bed, the raising of the sky without pillars, the sending of the messengers to make the way clear, as a call to it and a means of nearness to Him, the increase in creation, and the opening of the doors of provision. Then He drew attention to the chief of the favours, which is the oneness of the Benefactor, by His saying ﴿Is there any creator other than God﴾. The word "ghayru" is read in the nominative, as a qualifier, because "khaliqin" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is omitted, meaning "for you." It is read in the genitive by ʿAlī and Ḥamzah, as a qualifier in form (lafẓan).

﴿who provides for you﴾: it may be a resumed sentence (mustaʾnafah), and it may be a qualifier of "khaliq."

﴿from the sky﴾, by rain,

﴿and the earth﴾, by various kinds of plants.

﴿There is no god but Him﴾: a separate clause (jumlah mafṣūlah), having no place in i'rab.

﴿So how are you turned away?﴾: by what means are you diverted from monotheism to polytheism?!

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 4:**

(p-77) ﴿And if they deny you, then indeed messengers before you were denied﴾. With this, He rebukes the Quraysh for their poor reception of the signs of God and their denial of them, and He consoles His Messenger (ﷺ) by telling him that he has, among the prophets before him, a model to follow. For this reason He used the indefinite "messengers" (rusul), meaning: "messengers of great number, possessors of signs and warnings, people of long lifespans, and holders of patience and resolve." This is more consoling to him. The intended sense of the sentence is: "And if they deny you, then take consolation in the denial of the messengers before you," because the answer (jaza') follows the condition (shart). If it were taken in its outward order, the answer would come before the condition. So ﴿then indeed messengers before you were denied﴾ is placed in the position of "fa-ta'assa" (then take consolation), using the cause in place of the effect: the denial (al-takdhib) in place of the consolation (al-ta'assi).

﴿And to God are all matters returned﴾. This is a statement that includes both promise and threat, concerning the return of all matters to His judgment and the recompense of the one who denies and the one who is denied, according to what each deserves. "Turja'u" (are returned), with an open ta' (fatha), is the reading of Ibn 'Amir al-Shami, Hamzah, 'Ali, Ya'qub, Khalaf and Sahl.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 5:

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah﴾, that is, of resurrection and recompense,

﴿is true﴾, that is, it will certainly come to pass,

﴿so let not the worldly life deceive you﴾, that is, let not the world deceive you, nor let its enjoyment and its pleasures in its benefits distract you from working for the Hereafter and seeking what is with Allah,

﴿and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾, that is: Satan. For he holds out to you false hopes and says: Allah has no need of your worship, nor of your denial.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you﴾, an evident enmity. He did to your father what he did, and yet you treat him as one who has no knowledge of his circumstances.

﴿So take him as an enemy﴾, in your beliefs and your actions. Let there be nothing from you except what indicates opposition to him, in your private and your public conduct. Then he summarized the secret of his affair and refuted the one who follows him: that his aim, which he intends in calling his partisans (shi'ah), is to bring them to the place of ruin, by His saying: ﴿He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment﴾ [Fatir: 7].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 8:

﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good...﴾, through the adornment of Satan, the same as one for whom it has not been made attractive? It is as if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "No," and then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go to waste in regret over them﴾. Al-Zajjaj mentioned that the meaning is: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him...﴾ your soul has gone to waste in regret over him, and the answer has been omitted because of the indication of "فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ" (so do not let your soul go to waste) that follows it. Or [the meaning is]: "Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him like one whom Allah has guided?" and it has been omitted because of the indication of ﴿Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ upon it. "فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ" means: do not destroy it with regrets (حَسَراتٍ, "regrets," is an object of purpose, a maf'ul lahu, meaning: "do not destroy your soul for regrets"). "عَلَيْهِمْ" is a complement (صِلَة, here meaning the completing phrase) of "تَذْهَبْ," as you say: "he perished over him from love" and "he died over him from grief." It is not permissible for it to be connected to "حَسَراتٍ," because the verbal noun (مَصْدَر, masdar) may not have its complement placed before it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾: this is a warning (وَعِيد, wa'id, a threat) to them of punishment for the evil of their conduct.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 9:

﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds﴾, "al-riyah" (the winds). "Makki" (Ibn Kathir), "Hamzah" and "Ali" read it in the form "al-rih" (sing.)[?]

Note on the variant readings: the text here reads "اَلرِّيحَ" with a shadda on the ra' and is given as the reading of Makki, Hamza and Ali.

﴿so that they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land﴾, with the emphatic form (tashdid), "Madani" (Abu Ja'far), "Hamzah", "Ali" and "Hafs" read it so; others read it with the light form (takhfif).

﴿And We revive thereby﴾, by the rain, since its mention has preceded implicitly,

﴿the earth after its death﴾, i.e., after its dryness. It was said: "fa-tuthir" (so they stir up), in order to depict the situation in which the stirring of clouds by the winds takes place, and to bring to mind that image which points to divine power. Thus they do with an act that carries a sense of distinction and particularity, in a circumstance that is considered strange. Likewise the driving of the clouds to a dead land and the reviving of the earth by rain after its death, because of the evidence it contains of overwhelming power. It was said: "fa-saqna" (We drove) and "ahyayna" (We revived), with both shifted away from the third-person form to what is more fitting for particularity and more indicative of it,

﴿Thus is the resurrection﴾, the kaf (ka) is in the place of nominative case, meaning: like the reviving of dead land is the resurrection of the dead. It was said: Allah revives creation by water which He sends from beneath the Throne, like the semen of men, from which the bodies of creation grow.

The commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 35, verse 10:

﴿Whoever desires honor, then all honor belongs to Allah.﴾ That is: all honor is exclusively Allah's, the honor of this world and the honor of the Hereafter. The disbelievers used to seek strength through the idols, as He said: ﴿And they took besides Allah gods, that they might be for them a source of honor.﴾ [Maryam: 81]. Those who believed with their tongues, without their hearts agreeing, used to seek strength through the polytheists, as He said: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, honor belongs entirely to Allah.﴾ [al-Nisa: 139]. Thus He made clear that there is no honor except with Allah. The meaning is: let him seek it from Allah. The statement ﴿to Allah belongs all honor﴾ was placed in the position of the omitted clause, being sufficient in its place because it indicates it, since a thing is sought only from its owner and possessor. A parallel is your saying: "Whoever desires counsel, it is with the righteous," meaning: let him seek it from them, except that you have put what indicates it in its place.

In a hadith: "Indeed your Lord says every day: 'I am the Mighty (al-'Aziz), so whoever desires the honor of both abodes, let him obey the Mighty.'"

Then He specified that what honor is sought through is faith and righteous deeds, by His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it.﴾ The meaning of His words "to Him" is: to the place of acceptance and pleasure. Whatever is characterized by acceptance is described as elevated and ascending, or it means: to where none but His command takes effect. "Al-kalim al-tayyib" (the good word) means the words of tawhid, that is: there is no god but Allah. The analogical form would be "al-tayyibah" (feminine singular), but every plural whose only difference from its singular is the taa' marker may be treated as masculine or feminine. "Al-'amal al-salih" (righteous deed) means pure worship. The meaning is: "And the good word raises the righteous deed." Here the raiser (al-rafi') is "al-kalim" (the word), and the one raised (al-marfu') is "al-'amal" (the deed), because no deed is accepted except from one who professes tawhid.

It has also been said: the raiser is Allah, and the one raised is "al-'amal," meaning: "the righteous deed is raised by Allah." This contains an indication that the deed depends on being raised, whereas the good word ascends by itself.

It has also been said: the righteous deed raises the doer and honors him, meaning: whoever desires honor, let him perform a righteous deed, for it is that which raises the servant.

﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾: this is an attribute of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), meaning: (p-٨٠) "the evil plots." This is because "makara" is an intransitive verb, and one does not say "so-and-so plotted his deed." The intended referent is the plot of the Quraysh against him (ﷺ) when they gathered in Dar al-Nadwa, as Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30], and the verse continues.

﴿For them is a severe punishment﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿And the plot of those﴾: a subject (mubtada').

﴿It﴾: a separating pronoun (damir al-fasl).

﴿will perish﴾: a predicate (khabar). That is: "And the plot of those who plotted, it alone, will perish." That is: it will decay and come to nothing, unlike the plot of Allah against them, when He expelled them from Mecca, killed them, and cast them into the well of Badr. Thus He gathered their plots against them all together, and fulfilled in them His saying (Exalted): ﴿And they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal: 30], and His saying: ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

﴿And Allah created you﴾, i.e., your father [Adam],

﴿from dust, then﴾ brought you into being [from dust],

﴿from a drop of semen, then He made you into pairs﴾, i.e., kinds, or males and females,

﴿And no female bears or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾. Here (*wa-ma taḥmilu*) is in the position of a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, a term for an adverbial phrase describing the state of the subject at the time of the action), meaning: except that it is known to Him,

﴿And no one is granted a long life﴾, i.e., no one at all is granted a long life. He is called "one granted a long life" because of what he is heading toward,

﴿nor is any of his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾, meaning the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ*) or the record of the person's deeds. "Nor is shortened" [is in the form of] "Zayd" [i.e., the verb is in the third-person singular, like *zaydun* as a grammatical example of a noun, used here to illustrate that the verb agrees with its subject]. If you say: a person is either "one granted a long life," meaning long-lived, or "one whose life is shortened," meaning short-lived; it is impossible for granting length and its opposite to apply to the same person in succession. How then is the statement correct, "And no one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened"? I say: this is a form of speech that is lenient in its wording, relying on the hearers' understanding of its interpretation and on their reasoning to grasp its meaning, and because it is not unclear to them that a lifespan cannot be both long and short at once. This is also how people speak, saying: "God does not reward or punish a servant except with right," [meaning the statement is understood within its proper context]. Or the interpretation of the verse is that He writes in the record: "His life is so-and-so many years," then He writes at the bottom of that: "A day has passed, two days have passed," until it reaches its end. That is the shortening of his life. From Qatada: "The one granted a long life" is the one who reaches sixty years, and "the one whose life is shortened" is the one who dies before sixty years.

﴿Indeed, that﴾, i.e., its recording, or the lengthening or shortening of life,

﴿for Allah is easy﴾, simple.

﴿وَما يَسْتَوِي البَحْرانِ هَذا﴾ means: "And the two seas are not alike." It means that one of them,

﴿عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ﴾ "sweet and fresh," meaning extremely sweet. It is said that it is the kind that quenches thirst.

﴿سائِغٌ شَرابُهُ﴾ "pleasant to drink," meaning easy to swallow and easy to go down, because of its sweetness, and by it its drink is raised up.

﴿وَهَذا مِلْحٌ أُجاجٌ﴾ "and this one is salty and bitter," meaning extremely salty. It is said that it is the kind that burns with its saltiness.

﴿وَمِن كُلٍّ﴾ "and from each," meaning from each one of the two.

﴿تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا﴾ "you eat fresh flesh," which is fish.

﴿وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها﴾ "and you extract ornaments that you wear," which are pearls and coral.

﴿وَتَرى الفُلْكَ فِيهِ﴾ "and you see the ships in it," meaning in each of them.

﴿مَواخِرَ﴾ "plowing through," meaning cutting through the water by their movement. It is said: "مَخَرَتِ السَفِينَةُ الماءَ" (the ship plowed the water), meaning it cut through it, and it is ماخِرَةٌ (a ship that plows).

﴿لِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ "that you may seek of His bounty," meaning of the bounty of Allah. There was no mention of this in the verse, but it is mentioned in what precedes it. Had it not been mentioned, it would not have been unclear, because the meaning points to it.

﴿وَلَعَلَّكم تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ "and perhaps you will be grateful," to Allah, for what He has given you of His bounty. He has struck the two seas, the sweet and the salty, as two parables for the believer and the disbeliever. Then he said, by way of digression (istitrad, a shift to another topic before returning to the main one) in describing the two seas and what is attached to them of His blessing and bounty, and it may bear a meaning other than the path of istitrad, which is that he likens the two kinds to the two seas, and then prefers the bitter sea to the disbeliever in that it shares with the sweet sea in benefits, such as fish, pearls, and the sailing of ships in it, whereas the disbeliever is devoid of benefit. So it is in the manner of His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكم مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَهي كالحِجارَةِ أوْ أشَدُّ قَسْوَةً﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 74] "Then your hearts hardened after that, so they were like stones or even harder in hardness." Then He said: ﴿وَإنَّ مِنَ الحِجارَةِ لَما يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنهُ الأنْهارُ وإنَّ مِنها لَما يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنهُ الماءُ وإنَّ مِنها لَما يَهْبِطُ مِن خَشْيَةِ اللهِ﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 74] "Indeed, of stones there are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed of them there are those that split and water comes out of them, and indeed of them there are those that fall down out of fear of Allah" -:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾: He takes from the hours of each of them and inserts them into the other, until the longer of the two becomes fifteen hours and the shorter becomes nine,

﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾: that is, He made the most luminous of forms subject to the most laborious of courses,

﴿each runs for a specified term﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection their running will come to an end.

﴿That﴾ is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence),

﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the kingdom﴾: these are successive khabars (predicates), or: "Allah is your Lord" is the khabar of inna (the emphatic particle), and "to Him belongs the kingdom" is a mubtada' clause. It occurs in the context of His words: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾, meaning the idols you worship besides Allah. "Yad'una" (they call upon), read by Qutayba, [is a variant reading].

﴿do not possess even a qitmir﴾: it is the thin skin that wraps around the date-stone (pit).

(p-82)

"If you call upon them" — that is, the idols — "they do not hear your call," because they are inanimate objects. "And even if they heard," by way of supposition, "they would not answer you," because they do not claim the divinity you claim for them, and they disavow it. "And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association," that is, your associating them with God and your worshipping them. They will say: "You did not use to worship us" [Yunus 10:28]. "And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware" — and none can inform you, O you who are deluded by the causes of delusion, as the All-Aware God informs you, the One who knows the hidden secrets of affairs. Its real meaning is: "No informant can inform you of the matter who is like one who is aware of it," meaning that only the one who has true knowledge of the matter is the one who informs you of the reality, not the other informants about it. The meaning is that what I have told you about the state of the idols is the truth, because I am aware of what I have informed you about.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 15:

﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah﴾. Dhu al-Nun (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The creation is in need of Him in every breath, every passing thought, and every glance. And how could it not be, when their existence is through Him and their continuance is through Him?! ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient﴾, free of all things,

﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, who is praised by every tongue. He did not name them "the poor" to belittle them; rather, it is an indication of the (need for) self-sufficiency. For this reason He described Himself as "the Self-Sufficient," who is the one who feeds the wealthy, and He mentioned "the Praiseworthy," to show by it that He is the self-sufficient who benefits His creation through His self-sufficiency, and the bountiful who bestows favours upon them. For not every self-sufficient person benefits others by his wealth, unless the self-sufficient one is generous and bountiful. And when he gives generously and bestows favours, the one upon whom he bestows favours praises him. Sahl said: When Allah created the creation, He decreed self-sufficiency for Himself and poverty for them. Whoever claims self-sufficiency is veiled from Allah, and whoever displays his poverty, his poverty brings him to Him. It is fitting for the servant to be inwardly in need of Him and cut off from others in turning to Him, until his servanthood is pure. Servanthood is humility and submission, and its sign is that he does not ask anyone. Al-Wasiti said: "Whoever is self-sufficient through Allah will not become poor, and whoever is honoured through Allah will not be humiliated." Al-Husayn said: In proportion to the servant's need of Allah, he becomes self-sufficient through Allah, and the more he increases in need, the more he increases in self-sufficiency. Yahya said: Poverty is better for the servant than wealth, because humiliation is in poverty and arrogance is in wealth, and returning to Allah with humility and lowliness is better than returning to Him by multiplying deeds. It was said: The attributes of the friends of Allah are three: trust in Allah in all things, need of Him in all things, and turning to Him from all things. Al-Shibli said: Poverty draws trial, and all of its trial is honour.

﴿If He wills, He will take you away﴾, all of you, into non-existence, for His self-sufficiency (ghina) is in His essence, not in you, from eternity (al-qidam),

﴿and bring a new creation﴾, and He, without your praise, is Praiseworthy (hamid).

"And that," the bringing into being and the annihilation, ﴿is not difficult for Allah﴾, meaning, not impossible. And from Ibn ʿAbbas: He will create after you those who will worship Him and not associate anything with Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 35, verse 18:

﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ No soul that bears sin shall bear the sin of another soul. *Al-wizr* (الوِزْر) and *al-wiqr* (الوَقْر) are brothers in meaning. *Wazara al-shay'* (وَزَرَ الشيءَ) means he carried the thing. *Al-wazira* (الوازِرَة) is an adjective describing *nafs* (soul). The meaning is that on the Day of Resurrection every soul will carry only the burden of what it committed. No soul will be held to account for another soul's sin, as the tyrants of this world seize a close relative for a close relative, or a neighbour for a neighbour. The reason it says *wazira* (وازِرَة) and not "no soul bears the burden of another," is that the meaning is that none of the souls that bear burdens is seen carrying anything but its own burden, not the burden of someone else.

As for His words, ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and other burdens along with their own burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13], this refers to those who go astray and lead others astray. They carry the burdens of misguiding people along with the burdens of their own misguidance. All of that is their own burdens, and there is nothing in it of the burden of anyone else. Do you not see how Allah (exalted is He) refuted them in their saying, ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 12], with His words, ﴿but they will not bear anything of their sins at all﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 12].

﴿And if a burdened soul calls out for its load﴾, that is, a soul weighed down with sins, calls on someone, ﴿for its load﴾, its weight, that is, its sins, so that someone might carry some of that for it, (p. 84) ﴿nothing of it will be carried, even if it were﴾, that is, the one being called upon, which is understood from His words, "and if a burdened soul calls out," ﴿a near relative﴾, one of close kinship, such as a father, a son, or a brother.

The difference between the meaning of His words, "No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another," and the meaning of "And if a burdened soul calls out for its load, nothing of it will be carried," is that the first indicates the justice of Allah in His judgement, and that He does not hold a soul accountable for a sin it did not commit. The second explains that on that day there is no one to give relief to one who seeks help. So even if a soul has been weighed down by its burdens, and it calls out for some of its heavy load to be lightened, it will not be answered and will not be relieved, even if the one called upon is one of its close relatives.

﴿You warn only those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, that is, only these people benefit from your warning.

﴿Unseen﴾ (*bil-ghayb*, بِالغَيْبِ) is a circumstantial qualifier (*ḥāl*, حال) relating either to the subject or the object. That is, they fear their Lord while absent from His punishment, or they fear His punishment while it is absent from them. It has also been said that "unseen" means in private, where no one else can observe them.

﴿And they establish the prayer﴾, at its appointed times.

﴿And whoever purifies himself﴾, cleanses himself by performing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience.

﴿purifies himself only for his own sake﴾. This is an interjected statement that emphasises their fear of Allah and their establishing of the prayer, because both are part of purification.

﴿And to Allah is the final destination﴾, the return. This is a promise of reward for the one who purifies himself.

The blind and the seeing are not equal (Qur'an 35:19). It is a parable for the disbeliever and the believer, or for the ignorant and the knowledgeable.

Wait, I must correct my own rendering: "disbelievers" is the correct plural, and I should not have written "disbelieveer." The corrected translation follows.

The blind and the seeing are not equal. This is a parable (mathal) for the disbeliever and the believer, or for the ignorant and the knowledgeable.

﴿Nor are the darknesses﴾, an example for disbelief,

﴿nor the light﴾, for faith.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 21:

﴿Nor is the shade [equal to] the scorching heat.﴾ [That is:] the truth and falsehood, or Paradise and Hellfire. And "al-harur" (the scorching wind): a hot wind like the samum (the poisonous, scorching wind), except that the samum occurs by day, whereas the harur occurs by night and by day, according to al-Farra'.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 22:

﴿And the living and the dead are not alike.﴾ It is a parable for those who have entered Islam and those who have not entered it. The repetition of "lā" (not) serves to emphasize the meaning of negation. The difference between these waws is that some of them join an even pair to another even pair, and some join an odd to an odd.

﴿Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves.﴾ It means that He knows who will enter Islam from among those who will not enter it, so He guides whom He wills to guidance. As for you, their affair is hidden from you, and so you are eager for the Islam of a people who are forsaken. He likened the disbelievers to the dead, since they do not benefit from what they hear.

Qur'an 35:23: ﴿You are only a warner.﴾ That is: your only duty is to convey and to warn. If the one warned is among those who listen to the warning, it benefits him; and if he is among the obstinate, then you bear no blame.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 25:

﴿And if they deny you, those before them had also denied, their messengers,﴾

﴿their messengers came to them﴾: a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), with "qad" (indeed) implied (muḍmara).

﴿with the clear proofs﴾: with the miracles (al-mu'jizāt).

﴿and with the scriptures﴾: and with the sheets (al-ṣuḥuf).

﴿and with the illuminating Book﴾: that is, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms (al-Zabūr). Since these things were within their kind (jins), the coming of them was attributed to them in an unrestricted attribution (isnād muṭlaq), even though some of them were in all of them, namely the clear proofs, and some were in some of them, namely the scriptures and the Book. In this there is consolation (maslāh) for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 26:

﴿Then I seized﴾, i.e., I punished,

﴿those who disbelieved﴾, with various kinds of punishment,

﴿so how was My disapproval﴾, i.e., My rejection of them and My chastisement of them.

(p-86) ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby﴾, by the water,

﴿fruits of diverse colors﴾, meaning their kinds, such as pomegranates, apples, figs, grapes, and others, which cannot be counted; or their forms, such as redness, yellowness, greenness, and the like,

﴿And of the mountains are streaks﴾, paths of varying color, the plural of "judda" (jaddah), like "mudda" and "mudad,"

﴿white and red, of diverse colors, and deep black﴾, the plural of "gharibib" (ghirbib), which is an intensifier of "black." It is said: "aswad gharibib" (intensely black), meaning one who has gone far in blackness and become extremely so. From this comes "al-ghurab" (the crow). By right, an intensifier should follow the word it intensifies, as in your saying "asfar faqi'" (bright yellow). However, the intensified word has been omitted before it, and what follows it serves as an explanation of the omitted term. This is done only to increase emphasis, since it indicates a single meaning through both the expressed and the implied forms together. In His saying ﴿And of the mountains are streaks﴾ it is necessary to assume an omitted genitive (mudaf): i.e., "And of the mountains are those having streaks, white, red, and black," so that it returns to the meaning "And of the mountains are those whose colors are diverse," as He said: ﴿fruits of diverse colors﴾.

﴿And among people, beasts, and livestock are those whose colors vary﴾. (That is,) among them is some whose colors vary.

﴿Likewise﴾, i.e., like the variation of the fruits and the mountains. When He said, ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky?﴾ [Fatir: 27], and enumerated the signs of Allah, the indicators of His power, the traces of His craftsmanship, and the diverse kinds of creation that point to Him and to His attributes, He followed that with: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾, i.e., those who have knowledge of Him, who know Him through His attributes, and so glorify Him. The more one increases in knowledge of Him, the more one increases in fear of Him, and whoever has less knowledge of Him is more secure. In a hadith: "The one among you who knows Allah best is the one who fears Him most." The placement of the name of Allah (Exalted) first and the placement of "the scholars" last indicates that the meaning is that those who fear Him among His servants are the scholars, and not others. Had the order been reversed, the meaning would have been that they fear none but Allah, as in His saying: ﴿And they fear no one except Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39]. Between the two there is a difference: in the first, there is a statement that the ones who fear are the scholars; in the second, there is a statement that the one feared is Allah (Exalted). Abu Hanifa, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Ibn Sirin (may Allah be pleased with them) read: "Only Allah fears among His servants the scholars" (with ʿulamāʾa in the accusative). In this recitation, "fear" (al-khashya) is a metaphor (istiʿara), and the meaning is: Allah magnifies among His servants the scholars.

﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty, Oft-Forgiving﴾: this is a justification for the obligation of fear, because it indicates His punishment of the disobedient, His subjugation of them, His reward for the people of obedience, and His pardon of them. The one who punishes and the one who rewards has the right to be feared.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾: they persevere in the recitation of the Qur'an.

﴿and establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾: that is, they keep voluntary spending (nafl) secret and make obligatory spending (fard) public. The meaning is that they are not content with mere recitation of it, [without] the sweetness of acting upon it.

﴿hope﴾: this is the predicate (khabar) of "inna" (indeed).

﴿for a commerce﴾: it is the seeking of reward through obedience.

﴿that will never perish﴾: that will never be unprofitable (takassud), meaning a commerce from which slump is absent and which will not fail (tanfuq) with Allah.

﴿That He may pay them in full﴾: this is connected to "will never perish." That is, by their spending for His sake, He pays them their rewards, the reward of their deeds,

﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾: by widening their graves, or by granting them intercession for those who were good to them, or by multiplying their good deeds, or by fulfilling the promise of meeting Him. Or "yarjūna" (they hope) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial clause), meaning "hoping." The lām in "liyuwaffiyahum" is connected to "yatlūna" (they recite) and what follows it, meaning: they did all of that, the recitation, the establishment of prayer, and spending for this purpose. The predicate of "inna" (indeed) is:

﴿Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾: that is, Forgiving toward them, and Appreciative of their deeds, meaning He gives abundantly for little work.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 31:

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an. The "min" (مِن) here is for explanation (lit-tabyin) —

﴿is the truth, confirming﴾ — a circumstantial qualifier (hal) that is emphatic (mu'akkidah), because the truth is never separated from this confirmation —

﴿what is before it﴾ (lima bayna yadayh) — i.e., the books that came before it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾ — He knew you and saw your circumstances, and saw you as fit to have revealed to you a book like this, the inimitable one, which is a criterion (ʿiyar) over all the other books.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 32:

﴿ثُمَّ أوْرَثْنا الكِتابَ﴾ means: We revealed the Qur'an to you, then We made it an inheritance from after you, i.e., We decreed its inheritance.

﴿الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِن عِبادِنا﴾ refers to his community (ummah): the Companions, the Successors (al-Tabi'un), those who followed the Successors, and those after them until the Day of Resurrection. This is because Allah chose them over all other nations, made them a middle community (ummah wasatan) so that they would be witnesses over mankind, and singled them out with the honour of belonging to the best of His messengers. Then He arranged them into ranks, saying: ﴿فَمِنهم ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ ("Among them is one who wrongs himself"), and this is the one whose matter is deferred (al-Murja') to the command of Allah.

﴿وَمِنهم مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾ ("and among them is one who is moderate") is the one who mixed a righteous deed with an evil one.

﴿وَمِنهم سابِقٌ بِالخَيْراتِ﴾ ("and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds"). This interpretation agrees with the revelation, for He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿والسابِقُونَ الأوَّلُونَ مِنَ المُهاجِرِينَ﴾ ("And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants") [at-Tawbah: 100], etc., and after it said: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ اعْتَرَفُوا بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ ("And others who have acknowledged their sins") [at-Tawbah: 102], etc., and after it said: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لأمْرِ اللهِ﴾ ("And others deferred to the command of Allah") [at-Tawbah: 106], etc. It also agrees with the hadith. It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that, on the pulpit, after reciting this verse, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Our foremost is foremost, our moderate one is saved, and our one who wrongs himself is forgiven." And from him (ﷺ): "The foremost enters Paradise without reckoning, the moderate one is reckoned with an easy reckoning and then enters Paradise, and as for the one who wrongs himself, he will be held back until he thinks he will not be saved; then mercy will reach him and he will enter Paradise." This was narrated by Abu al-Darda'. It also agrees with the report from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): The foremost is the sincere one, the moderate one is the hypocrite, and the one who wrongs himself is the one who disbelieves in the blessing but does not deny Him, because He judged all three to enter Paradise. It also agrees with the statement of the early generation (al-Salaf). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The one who wrongs himself is the possessor of major sins, the moderate one is the possessor of minor sins, and the foremost is the one who avoids both. al-Hasan al-Basri said: The one who wrongs himself is the one whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds; the foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds; and the moderate one is the one whose good and evil deeds are equal. Abu Yusuf (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked about this verse and said: "All of them are believers, and the description of the disbelievers comes after this, which is His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهم نارُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ ("But those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell") [Fatir: 36]." As for the three categories, they are those whom He chose from among His servants, for He said: "Among them... and among them... and among them...", and all of it refers back to His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِن عِبادِنا﴾, and they are the people of faith (ahl al-iman). This is the view of the majority (al-Jumhur).

He mentioned the one who wrongs himself first to indicate their great number, and that the moderate ones are few in comparison to them, and the foremost are fewer than the few. Ibn 'Ata' said: He mentioned the one who wrongs himself first so that he would not despair of His grace. It was also said: He mentioned him first to make him know that his sin does not distance him from his Lord. It was also said: The first state is disobedience, then repentance, then steadfastness.

Sahl said: The foremost is the scholar, the moderate one is the learner, and the one who wrongs himself is the ignorant. He also said: The foremost is the one occupied with his hereafter; the moderate one is the one occupied with his livelihood and his hereafter; and the one who wrongs himself is the one occupied with his livelihood to the neglect of his hereafter.

It was also said: The one who wrongs himself is the one who worships Him out of heedlessness and habit; the moderate one is the one who worships Him out of desire and fear; and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe and a sense of His due right. It was also said: The one who wrongs himself is the one who takes the world, whether lawful or unlawful; the moderate one is the one who strives not to take it except from what is lawful; and the foremost is the one who turns away from it entirely. It was also said: The one who wrongs himself is the seeker of this world; the moderate one is the seeker of the reward (al-'Uqba) ; and the foremost is the seeker of the Master (al-Mawla).

﴿بِإذْنِ اللهِ﴾ means: by His command, or by His knowledge, or by His enabling success (tawfiq).

﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ refers to the inheriting of the Book.

﴿هُوَ الفَضْلُ الكَبِيرُ﴾ ("That is the great bounty").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 33:

﴿Gardens of perpetual residence (jannatu ʿadn)﴾: it is a second predicate (khabar thani) of "dhalika" (that), or the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf), or it is itself a subject (mubtada'). The predicate is: ﴿they will enter them﴾, i.e., the three groups. "Yudkhalunaha" (they will be made to enter them): Abu ʿAmr (reading).

﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets﴾: the plural of "asawira", which is the plural of "siwar" (bracelet).

﴿of gold and pearls﴾: i.e., of gold set with pearls. "Wa-lu'lu'an" (and pearls), in the accusative with a hamza: Nafiʿ and Hafs. They conjoined it to the position (mahall) of "min asawira" (of bracelets), i.e., "they will be adorned with bracelets and pearls."

﴿And their clothing therein will be silk﴾, because of the pleasure and adornment it contains.

The Qur'anic quotations are rendered with their meaning, and the grammatical discussion is translated with the Arabic words kept in script.

﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence﴾, i.e., al-Iqamah (the abode of lasting residence), where we will not depart from it nor be separated from it. It is said: "aqamtu iqamatan, wa muqaman, wa muqamah" (I stayed/resided, with three verbal nouns).

﴿out of His bounty﴾, from His gift and His favours, not by our own merit.

﴿No fatigue touches us therein﴾, toil and hardship.

﴿Nor does weariness touch us therein﴾, exhaustion resulting from toil, and a lapse of strength. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read "لَغُوبٌ" (lughub) with a fatha on the lam, and it is that by which one becomes exhausted, i.e., we will not undertake any labour that would exhaust us.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 36:

﴿And as for those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. They will not be given a decree to die, so that they would die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them.﴾ It is the response (jawab) to the negation, and its being in the subjunctive (nasb) is due to the implicit "an" (that), meaning: "They will not be given a decree of a second death, so that they would rest."

﴿And its punishment will not be lightened for them﴾, that is, the punishment of the fire of Hell.

﴿Thus﴾, like that recompense,

﴿We recompense every ingrate (kafur)﴾, "every ingrate is recompensed" (yujza), [a reading] of Abu 'Amr.

﴿وَهم يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها﴾ [while they cry out therein]: يَسْتَغِيثُونَ [they call for help]. فَهو "يَفْتَعِلُونَ" [yaftaʿilūna, a verb of the form VIII (ifti‘āl)], مِن "اَلصُّراخُ" [from al-ṣurākh, "shouting"], وهو الصِياحُ بِجُهْدٍ ومَشَقَّةٍ [which is shouting with strain and effort], واسْتُعْمِلَ في الِاسْتِغاثَةِ لِجَهْرِ صَوْتِ المُسْتَغِيثِ [and it is used for calling for help because of the raising of the voice of the one calling for help].

﴿رَبَّنا﴾ [Our Lord], يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنا [they say: "Our Lord"],

﴿أخْرِجْنا نَعْمَلْ صالِحًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنّا نَعْمَلُ﴾ [Bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do]. أيْ: أخْرِجْنا مِنَ النارِ، رُدَّنا إلى الدُنْيا، نُؤْمِن بَدَلَ الكُفْرِ، ونُطِعْ بَعْدَ المَعْصِيَةِ [That is: bring us out of the Fire, return us to the world, that we may believe instead of disbelieving and obey after disobedience], فَيُجاوَبُونَ بَعْدَ قَدْرِ عُمُرِ الدُنْيا: ﴿أوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكم ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ﴾ [so they are answered, after the span of the life of the world: "Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would remember could remember therein?"]، يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ "ما"، نَكِرَةً مَوْصُوفَةً [it is permissible for "mā" to be an indefinite noun (nakira) with a descriptive clause (mawṣūfa), i.e., a term qualified by the clause that follows it]، أيْ: تَعْمِيرًا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ [meaning: a lifespan in which whoever would remember could remember]، وهو مُتَناوِلٌ لِكُلِّ عُمُرٍ تَمَكَّنَ مِنهُ المُكَلَّفُ مِن إصْلاحِ شَأْنِهِ، وإنْ قَصُرَ [and it includes every lifespan in which the responsible person was able to set his affairs right, even if it was short]، إلّا أنَّ التَوْبِيخَ في المُتَطاوِلِ أعْظَمُ [except that the rebuke is greater for a long lifespan]، ثُمَّ قِيلَ: هو ثَمانِيَ عَشَرَةَ سَنَةً، وقِيلَ: أرْبَعُونَ، وقِيلَ: سِتُّونَ سَنَةً [then it was said: it is eighteen years; it was said: forty; it was said: sixty years].

﴿وَجاءَكُمُ النَذِيرُ﴾ [And the warner came to you], (p-٩١)اَلرَّسُولُ ﷺ [the Messenger (ﷺ)]، أوِ المَشِيبُ [or grey hair], وهو عَطْفٌ عَلى مَعْنى "أوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ" [and it is a coordination (ʿaṭf) with the meaning of "Did We not give you a life long enough", i.e., it is linked to the sense of the phrase rather than its form]، لِأنَّ لَفْظَهُ لَفْظُ اسْتِخْبارٍ، ومَعْناهُ إخْبارٌ [because its wording is that of a question (istikhbār), while its meaning is a statement (ikhbār)]، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: قَدْ عَمَّرْناكُمْ، وجاءَكُمُ النَذِيرُ، فَذُوقُوا العَذابَ [as if it were said: "We have certainly given you a long life, and the warner has come to you, so taste the punishment"].

﴿فَما لِلظّالِمِينَ مِن نَصِيرٍ﴾ [So the wrongdoers will have no helper]، ناصِرٍ يُعِينُهم [a helper who aids them].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 38:

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth,﴾ meaning: what is hidden in them from you.

﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾ This is in the manner of a reason given (ta'lil), because whoever knows what is in the breasts, which is the most hidden of things, has certainly known every unseen thing in the world. And "dhat al-sudur" (lit. "possessor of the breasts"): its concealed contents. It is the feminine form of "dhu" (possessor), as in the saying of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "Dhu baṭni Kharijata jariyah" (the one with the belly of Kharijah is a girl), meaning: what is in her belly of pregnancy, because pregnancy accompanies the belly; likewise, the concealed contents accompany the breasts. And "dhu" is laid down to express the meaning of companionship (ṣuḥbah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 39:

﴿He is the One who made you successors (khalā'if) upon the earth.﴾ It is said of the one who is made a successor: "khalīfah," and its plural is "khalā'if." The meaning is that He made you vicegerents (khulafā') in His land, having granted you the keys of disposal over it, given you authority over what is in it, and permitted you its benefits, so that you would thank Him through monotheism (tawhid) and obedience,

﴿So whoever disbelieves﴾ among you, and spurns such a noble favour,

﴿then upon him is his disbelief﴾: the burden of his disbelief returns upon him, and it is the abhorrence of God and the loss of the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿And the disbelievers' disbelief increases them in nothing but abhorrence in the sight of their Lord﴾, and it is the most intense hatred,

﴿And the disbelievers' disbelief increases them in nothing but loss﴾: ruin and perdition.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 40:

﴿Say: "Have you considered your partners,﴾ — your gods which you associated with Him in worship —

﴿those you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth.﴾ "Arūnī" (show me) is a substitute (badal) for "ara'aytum" (have you considered), because the meaning of "ara'aytum" is "inform me" (akhbirūnī), as if it were said: "Inform me about these partners and about what made them deserve partnership." (p-92) "Show me what part of the parts of the earth they independently created apart from Allah."

﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ Or do they have a partnership with Allah in the creation of the heavens?! ﴿Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear proof from it?﴾ That is: do they have with them a Book from Allah that states they are His partners, so that they stand upon proof and evidence from that Book?! "Bayyinātin" (clear proofs) is read by ʿAlī, Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr.

﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another﴾, what the wrongdoers promise — "baʿḍuhum" (one another) is a substitute (badal) for "al-ẓālimūn" (the wrongdoers), and they are the leaders —

﴿nothing but deception (ghurūran)﴾ — "baʿḍan" means the followers —

﴿except deception﴾, which is their saying: "These are our intercessors with Allah."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [to exist]﴾, He prevents them from ceasing, because holding back (al-imsak) is a preventing.

﴿And if they should cease﴾, on the assumption of a hypothetical case,

﴿if He were to hold them [back], none could hold them after Him﴾, none could hold them after His holding them. The first "min" (from) is extra (mazidah), for emphasizing the negation, and the second is for the beginning (li'l-ibtida', i.e. the starting point of the action),

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾, not hastening to punish, in that He holds them, although they were worthy of being crushed to pieces (tuhaddu hadda) because of the greatness of the word of shirk, as He said: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from it, and the earth splits open﴾ [Maryam: 90], etc.

﴿And they swore by God with the utmost of their oaths﴾. It is in the accusative as a *maṣdar* (verbal noun, i.e., an emphatic oath), meaning a forceful oath. It may also be in the accusative as a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative), meaning striving in their oaths.

﴿If a warner comes to them, they will surely be better guided than any one of the nations﴾. Quraysh had heard, before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), that the People of the Book (*Ahl al-Kitab*) had denied their messengers. So they said: "May God curse the Jews and Christians! Messengers came to them and they denied them. By God, if a messenger comes to us, we will surely be better guided than any one of the nations," meaning than the community of which it is said, "it is one of the nations," preferring it over others in guidance and uprightness. This is like saying of a great calamity, "it is one of the calamities."

﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, that is, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent,

﴿it only increased them in aversion﴾. That is, the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) only increased them in distance from the truth. This is a metaphorical attribution (*isnad majazi*), in which the action is ascribed to the cause rather than its agent.

(p-93) ﴿Arrogance in the land﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), and likewise ﴿and the evil plotting﴾. The meaning: "And it only increased them in aversion, due to arrogance and evil plotting." Or they are circumstantial (hal), meaning: "arrogant and plotting against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The original form of his saying "and the evil plotting" is: "and they plotted the evil [plotting]," i.e., "the evil plotting," then "and plotting the evil," then "and the evil plotting." The proof for this is His saying: ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass (la yahiq)—it surrounds and befalls—except its own people.﴾ Indeed it befell them on the day of Badr. And in the proverb: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it headfirst."

﴿Then do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?﴾ This is the sending down of punishment upon those who denied their messengers from the nations before them. The meaning: "Do they then await, after your denial, anything but that punishment will descend upon them like what descended upon those before them who denied the messengers?" He made their receiving of that a waiting for it from them.

﴿So you will not find any change in the way of Allah, nor will you find any alteration in the way of Allah.﴾ He explained that His way, which is the retribution against those who deny the messengers, is a way He does not change in its essence, nor does He shift it from its times, and that this is certainly to be carried out.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 44:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ He called them to witness by what they used to see during their journeys to al-Sham, Yemen and Iraq of the traces of those who passed away and the signs of their destruction and ruin.

﴿And they were stronger than them﴾, namely the people of Makkah, in power and capability, yet they could not escape.

﴿And Allah is not one to be frustrated﴾, that is, to be outpaced or escape Him, ﴿by anything﴾, any thing whatsoever,

﴿in the heavens or on earth. Indeed He is ever Knowing﴾ of them,

﴿Competent﴾, capable over them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 45:

﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task for what they have earned﴾, for the sins they have committed,

﴿He would not leave on its back﴾, on the back of the earth, because the mention of the earth occurred in His saying: (p-94) "Nor is there anything in the heavens or on the earth that could frustrate Him",

﴿any living creature﴾, any soul that crawls upon it,

﴿but He defers them until an appointed term﴾, until the Day of Resurrection,

﴿And when their term comes, then indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾, meaning: the reality of their affair and the wisdom of their judgment were not hidden from Him.
